title: Show, don't tell
brief:
The warehouse turns product descriptions into SKU codes using an unwritten house convention. Nobody can explain the rule, but here are known examples:

• Blue Cotton T-Shirt, size M → TSH-BLU-COT-M
• Black Leather Jacket, size L → JKT-BLK-LEA-L
• Red Wool Sweater, size S → SWT-RED-WOL-S

Teach the model the pattern so it outputs only the SKU.

lesson.summary: Some patterns are almost impossible to describe but trivial to demonstrate. Few-shot prompting puts 2–5 input → output examples directly in the prompt. The model infers both the rule and the exact output format from them.
lesson.why_it_matters: Few-shot is how teams adapt a general model like Granite to house conventions (codes, tone, labels) without fine-tuning.
lesson.strong_example:
Product: Blue Cotton T-Shirt, size M
SKU: TSH-BLU-COT-M

Product: Black Leather Jacket, size L
SKU: JKT-BLK-LEA-L

Product: {{product}}
SKU:

starter_prompt: Create a SKU code for this product: {{product}}

checks.label: Output is only a SKU, no extra text
Output is only a SKU, no extra text

hints: Could you explain the SKU rule in words precisely enough for a stranger? If not, how else could you communicate it?
This is few-shot prompting. When a pattern is easier to show than describe, include worked input → output examples in the prompt, formatted exactly how you want the answer.
Paste the three known examples into your prompt as 'Product: ... / SKU: ...' pairs, then end with 'Product: {{product}}' and 'SKU:', and say to output only the SKU.
reference_prompt:
Convert product descriptions into warehouse SKU codes. Follow the pattern in the examples exactly. Output only the SKU, nothing else.
